purpose: Dated gates the front office and the game builder use. Each date carries its source and whether it was knowable on the career date; a date marked projected is replaced by the actual only when its computation date is reached. Dates and rules only: no 2004-05 result is recorded.

status_values.derived: inferred from cited sources, reasoning given
status_values.design_choice: not verifiable for 2004-05; the simulation's documented choice

events.note: Team options, player options, qualifying offers and tenders are due.
events.source: Larry Coon, 1999 Salary Cap FAQ, Q34 (http://www.cbafaq.com/salarycap99.htm); library/2004/league/nba_2004_offseason_calendar.json

events.note: Free agents may negotiate with any club and agree in principle; nothing may be signed (except tenders, qualifying offers, first-round scale and second-round minimum signings) through July 13.
events.trades: no trade July 1-13 (inferred; see nba_1999_cba_rules.json trades.moratorium_trade_ban)

events.note: 2004-05 salary cap $43,870,000, tax line about $54.6 million, minimum team salary $32,900,000, mid-level exception $4,903,000, $1.6M exception; Charlotte cap $29,250,000. Effective July 14.
Moratorium over; contracts, offer sheets and trades may be signed.
Camps opened in the week of October 6, 2004 (sourced); the exact day is not stated, so Tuesday October 5 is the design choice. Up to 20 players under contract.
events.source: CBA press release, October 6, 2004: 'NBA Training Camps opened this week' (https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/nba-training-camp-rosters-feature-65-cba-alumni/n-3090807)

events.note: Preseason games, as far as the recorded schedule shows; the source omits games against non-NBA opponents and some neutral sites, so an earlier game cannot be ruled out.
Rosters cut to 15 (12 active, up to 3 on the injured list) before opening night; the deadline is taken as the day before the first game. The opening-day roster rule is unchanged from 2003-04.
Regular season begins; rosters at 15 (12 active, up to 3 on the injured list).
Ten-day contracts allowed from January 5, or the first business day after; January 5, 2005 was a Wednesday.

Last day a non-guaranteed player can be waived and clear waivers before the guarantee date: waivers take 48 hours during the season, so a January 7 release clears on January 9. Same rule as 2003-04 (runtime/roster_moves.py WAIVE_BY = 2004-01-07).
All contracts become guaranteed for the rest of the season; a player terminated on or after January 10 is owed the rest of the season's salary.
events.source: Larry Coon, 1999 Salary Cap FAQ, Q90 and Q96 (http://www.cbafaq.com/salarycap99.htm); library/2003/league/nba_1999_in_season_rules.json contract_guarantee_date

events.note: All-Star Weekend in Denver; the All-Star Game is Sunday February 20, 2005 at the Pepsi Center. No regular-season games February 18-21.
Trade deadline (Thursday). The 3 p.m. ET hour is carried from 2003-04 (derived).
events.source: UPI, February 24, 2005, 'Lots of action at NBA trade deadline' (https://www.upi.com/Sports_News/2005/02/24/Lots-of-action-at-NBA-trade-deadline/72021109289959/); https://www.basketball-reference.com/leagues/NBA_2005_transactions.html

events.note: A player waived after March 1 is ineligible for the playoff roster of any club that signs him for the rest of the season.
events.source: Larry Coon, 1999 Salary Cap FAQ, Q53 and Q96 (http://www.cbafaq.com/salarycap99.htm); library/2003/league/nba_1999_in_season_rules.json

events.note: Last regular-season games.
First-round games begin; four series open April 23 and four April 24. Bracket, seeding and dates: library/2004/league/nba_2004_05_playoff_rules.json.
NBA Finals window, 2-3-2: Game 1 June 9; Games 5-7, if needed, June 19, 21 and 23.
2005 NBA Draft (two rounds; last draft under the 1999 CBA's eligibility rules).
Team options, player options, qualifying offers and tenders for 2005-06 are due; the 1999 CBA expires the same day.
events.source: Larry Coon, 1999 Salary Cap FAQ, Q34 (http://www.cbafaq.com/salarycap99.htm); library/2005/league/nba_2005_cba_rules.json dates.agreement_in_principle

events.note: The 2004-05 tax line (about $54.6 million, published July 13, 2004) is applied only if league salaries exceed the trigger, which is computed after the season from league revenue. Whether it applies is not known before this date and must not be used earlier.
events.source: library/2004/league/nba_2004_offseason_calendar.json#luxury_tax_threshold_2004_05; date by analogy with the 2003-04 calendar

events.note: Free agents may negotiate and agree in principle; nothing may be signed. In 2005 the moratorium ran to August 1 because the new CBA (agreed in principle June 21, ratified July 30) had to be finalized; that extension is knowable only from June 21, 2005.
events.source: library/2005/league/nba_2005_cba_rules.json dates.july_moratorium_2005 (cbafaq05 Q93; UPI, July 30 and August 1, 2005)

events.note: Moratorium over; contracts and trades may be signed; the 2005-06 cap takes effect. Knowable only from the 2005 CBA agreement (June 21, 2005); before that the clock assumes the standard mid-July end.
Miami's team option on Wade's fourth season must be exercised by October 31 after his second season.
events.source: Larry Coon, 1999 Salary Cap FAQ, Q38 (extract line: 'this option must be exercised by October 31 after the player's second season'); library/2003/league/nba_2003_04_calendar.json
